raw.quick_summary: Two perpendicular planar vectors, u=(a,0) and v=(0,b), combine to form the resultant r=(a,b). The resultant length is given by the Pythagorean formula sqrt(a*a+b*b); with a=3 and b=4, the length is 5. Changing either component changes the geometry and resultant length, but no time-dependent motion is specified.

key_concepts.explanation: The vector u=(a,0) lies along the horizontal axis and has magnitude a.
The vector v=(0,b) lies along the vertical axis and has magnitude b.
u and v occupy perpendicular coordinate directions because one is horizontal and the other is vertical.
Adding u and v componentwise produces r=(a,b).
The magnitude of r is sqrt(a*a+b*b), obtained from the right-triangle relationship between the two components.
When a=3 and b=4, the resultant length is sqrt(3*3+4*4)=5.
Both a and b are restricted to values between 1 and 5.
Changing a or b changes the component arrows, the resultant arrow, and the triangle geometry.

nodes.label: Changing a or b changes the geometry

learning_path.title: From perpendicular components to resultant length
learning_path.reason: The source supports a short progression from identifying the component vectors, to forming the resultant, to calculating and exploring its magnitude.

steps.title: Identify the two component vectors
steps.learning_goal: Recognize the horizontal and vertical roles of u and v.
steps.explanation: u=(a,0) contributes only a horizontal component, while v=(0,b) contributes only a vertical component. Their directions are perpendicular.
steps.connection_to_previous: This is the foundation for interpreting the vector diagram and all later calculations.

steps.title: Form the resultant
steps.learning_goal: Combine the component vectors into one vector.
steps.explanation: Adding components coordinatewise gives r=u+v=(a,b). Geometrically, the two component arrows form the legs of a right triangle and r is the diagonal from the origin.
steps.connection_to_previous: Once the two components are identified, their coordinatewise sum defines the resultant.

steps.title: Calculate the resultant length
steps.learning_goal: Use the right-triangle formula to find the magnitude of r.
steps.explanation: Because the components are perpendicular, the resultant length is |r|=sqrt(a*a+b*b).
steps.connection_to_previous: The resultant vector from the previous step is the diagonal whose length must be calculated.

steps.title: Apply the 3-4-5 example and vary parameters
steps.learning_goal: Evaluate the formula and understand how a and b affect the geometry.
steps.explanation: For a=3 and b=4, |r|=sqrt(9+16)=5. Within the range 1≤a,b≤5, changing either parameter changes the corresponding component and generally changes the resultant geometry and length.
steps.connection_to_previous: The numerical example and parameter exploration directly apply the magnitude formula.
